correctness.rationale: For finite \(p\), the upper bound applies the exact scalar \(2\times2\) operator norm to each coordinate, sums \(p\)-th powers, and bounds the smaller output by half the sum. For the lower bound, a scalar maximizer exists by compactness and the two-coordinate vectors \((a,b)\) and \((b,-a)\) make the two Banach-space outputs equal to the scalar extremal norm. The \(p=\infty\) endpoint is handled separately. Symmetry of the matrix and standard operator duality give the Hölder-conjugate identity, while row/column sums and \(A^TA=(\lambda^2+\mu^2)I\) give the endpoint values. All hypotheses and endpoints are accounted for.

value.rationale: The result collapses a newly studied nonlinear two-vector Banach-space invariant on every real \(\ell_p\) sequence space to one standard \(2\times2\) operator norm. This is structural rather than a parameter-table recomputation: it proves dimension independence, a Hölder-duality symmetry, and exact endpoint values simultaneously. The reduction gives a direct route for future sharp evaluation or estimation of \(J_{\lambda,\mu}(\ell_p)\) using established finite-dimensional operator-norm methods.
